# Build the three data frames (per 100,000)
make_df <- function(dengue_vec, sle_vec) {
  data.frame(
    Country = names(dengue_vec),
    Dengue  = as.numeric(dengue_vec) * 100000,
    SLE     = as.numeric(sle_vec[names(dengue_vec)]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) |>
    mutate(Country = recode(Country, !!!display_label))
}

dengue_sle_adults <- make_df(dengue_adults, sle_adults)
dengue_sle_women  <- make_df(dengue_women,  sle_women)
dengue_sle_men    <- make_df(dengue_men,    sle_men)

cor_summary <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(Group = "Adults",
             Rho   = cor(dengue_sle_adults$Dengue, dengue_sle_adults$SLE, method = "spearman"),
             P     = cor.test(dengue_sle_adults$Dengue, dengue_sle_adults$SLE, method = "spearman")$p.value,
             N     = nrow(dengue_sle_adults)),
  data.frame(Group = "Women",
             Rho   = cor(dengue_sle_women$Dengue, dengue_sle_women$SLE, method = "spearman"),
             P     = cor.test(dengue_sle_women$Dengue, dengue_sle_women$SLE, method = "spearman")$p.value,
             N     = nrow(dengue_sle_women)),
  data.frame(Group = "Men",
             Rho   = cor(dengue_sle_men$Dengue, dengue_sle_men$SLE, method = "spearman"),
             P     = cor.test(dengue_sle_men$Dengue, dengue_sle_men$SLE, method = "spearman")$p.value,
             N     = nrow(dengue_sle_men))
) |>
  mutate(Rho = round(Rho, 3),
         P   = format.pval(P, digits = 3))

knitr::kable(
  cor_summary,
  caption = "Spearman Rank Correlation — global, by sex",
  col.names = c("Group", "Spearman's Rho", "P-value", "N countries")
)

# Dataset Curation and Selection 
```{r, results='asis'}
dataset_standards <- tribble(
  ~Standard, ~Dataset_ID, ~Description,
  
  "Lowest standard", "GSE43777", "0 controls + no gender",
  "Lowest standard", "GSE38246", "9 controls + no gender",
  "Lowest standard", "GSE17924", "0 controls + no gender",
  "Lowest standard", "GSE96656", "9 controls",
  
  "Gold standard", "GSE157240", "21 samples + 20 controls",
  "Gold standard", "GSE211567", "43 samples + 0 controls",
  "Gold standard", "PRJEB67470", "28 samples + 18 controls",
  
  "Silver Standard", "GSE178240", "88 samples + no controls + no gender",
  "Silver Standard", "GSE174482", "40 samples + no controls + no gender",
  "Silver Standard", "GSE279208", "16 samples + 10 controls + no gender",
  
  "Copper standard", "GSE40628", "14 samples + 6 controls + no gender",
  "Copper standard", "E-MTAB-3162", "30 samples + 15 controls no gender",
  "Copper standard", "GSE51808", "47 samples + 9 controls + no gender",
  "Copper standard", "GSE84331", "7 samples + 5 controls + no gender"
)


# Get a unique list of the standards in the order they appear
standards_list <- unique(dataset_standards$Standard)

# Loop through each standard
for (std in standards_list) {
  
  # 1. Print a large, styled HTML header for the group
  cat(sprintf("<h1 style='color: #2c3e50; border-bottom: 3px solid #2c3e50; padding-bottom: 5px; margin-top: 40px;'>%s</h1>\n", std))
  
  # 2. Filter the data for just this group
  group_data <- dataset_standards %>%
    filter(Standard == std) %>%
    select(Dataset_ID, Description)
  
  # 3. Create and print the table
  table_output <- kable(group_data, 
                        col.names = c("Dataset ID", "Sample Details"),
                        align = c("l", "l"),
                        format = "html") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), 
                  full_width = FALSE,
                  position = "left",
                  font_size = 14) %>%
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#f4f4f4") %>%
    column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, color = "#0056b3")
  
  print(table_output)
  
  # Add spacing between groups
  cat("<br><br>\n")
}
```

# Prof. Lourdes Peña-Castillo Question
<br>

###	Would  it be possible to do a cross-validation with MCO, so that it can be compared with machine learning approaches? For example, partition the data in k groups, run MCO in k-1 groups, use the best Pareto frontier to classify the group left out and then obtain performance metrics such as F1-score, precision and recall.
